answer_1.quote: In this paper, we propose a new evaluation toolkit for intent embedding models that measure their semantic understanding on two lingusitic phenomenon commonly observed in conversational systems-negation and implicature.

answer_2.quote: We first employ automatic metrics to understand the generated data. To achieve this, we use training set as reference and calculate BLEU , ROUGE-L , METEOR  and BertScore .

answer_3.quote: In Appendix A, we present a classification upper-bound on 10-shot multi-class classification with gpt-4-0613. We present gpt-4-0613 with the utterance and the top-5 predictions from instructor-large plus one ground truth label. We then ask the model to classify it into one of the class.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation centered around two questions: (1) "Can the utterance imply the intent?" (2) "If yes, is it conveyed explicitly?" We first sample 180 utterances containing 60 from original, 60 from negation and 60 from implicature. 8 human annotators from our internal team (with fluent English skills) provided binary answers for these two questions in a sequential manner.
answer_4.guideline: Task 1: Determine whether an utterance may (or can) correctly imply a given intent. Task 2: If yes, determine whether the intent is conveyed explicitly.
